summary_paragraph: A 30-year-old woman with Type 1 diabetes and gastroparesis was admitted for recurrent intractable nausea and vomiting, unable to tolerate oral intake. She was managed with NPO status, IV fluids, and antiemetics including ondansetron, prochlorperazine, and lorazepam. Her blood glucose was elevated with ketonuria, prompting an increase in her Lantus dose from 28 to 31 units and adjustment of her sliding scale insulin. Hypertension, likely exacerbated by acute illness, was treated with IV hydralazine and transitioned to oral lisinopril 20 mg daily and metoprolol 50 mg twice daily. A CT head with contrast showed no central cause for her symptoms. Her nausea resolved, diet was advanced successfully, and she remained stable. She was discharged home with medication changes and instructions to follow up with her primary care provider and endocrinologist.
problems: Diabetes with neurological manifestations, type I [juvenile type], uncontrolled
